thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: INC-2026-4027 fired for prod-gen-1 — repeated GPU driver resets and OOMs reported on multiple containers

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert: trigger=GPU-Driver-Reset, severity=high, service=prod-inference, incident=PDR-4027 (link: https://pd.example.com/incidents/PDR-4027)

Alex: acked on-call, I'm up. seeing lots of CUDA OOM / driver reset logs from model-worker pods in prod-gen-1.

Maya: confirmed. k8s events show kubelet marking nodes NotReady after driver reset on gpu-node-09 and gpu-node-11.

Jordan: logs from model-worker-5: ```E CUDA: driver reset detected
E cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (size=268435456)
W falling back to error handler
```

Sam: are we seeing KV cache evictions or just raw alloc fails?

Maya: both. High KV cache churn + alloc failures. KV cache hit rate dropping from 92% -> 40% in last 12m.

Lee: customer impact: a few high-traffic tenants (tenant-a, tenant-b) reporting 503s and >5s tail latency for streaming responses. Status page updated to "degraded" for inference. link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/PD-4027

Alex: immediate mitigation: 1) remove GPU load from affected nodes 2) enable fallback model (cpu-quant) for sensitive routes 3) open ticket to infra for driver investigation. I'll start 1 & 2 now.

Maya: commands I'm running: ```# cordon & drain gpu-node-09 and gpu-node-11 kubectl cordon gpu-node-09 && kubectl drain gpu-node-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n prodkubectl cordon gpu-node-11 && kubectl drain gpu-node-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n prod```

Maya: also scaling up dedicated fallback pool: ```./opsctl scale-pool --name=cpu-fallback-1 --replicas=10 --region=us-west-2```

Sam: I've flipped the routing rule for tenant-b to use cpu-fallback-1 for critical routes. patch: ```curl -X POST https://ops-api/routing -d '{"route":"tenant-b/stream","pool":"cpu-fallback-1"}'```

Jordan: collecting dmesg and /var/log/messages from gpu-node-09: ```[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.```. Looks like driver crash (Xid 79) precedes the OOMs.

Alex: good catch. Xid 79 implies GPU hardware/driver fault, not just allocation pressure. Escalating to infra and drivers. @Maya can you open infra PD ticket PDR-4027-DRIVER with logs attached?

Maya: on it. created infra ticket: https://infra-tickets.example/TKT-8743. added kernel/dmesg, container logs, node metrics snapshot.

Lee: Customer comms: Sent notice to tenant-a and tenant-b that we're investigating GPU driver resets and that we routed critical traffic to fallback to reduce errors. Asked for any urgent jobs to be paused.

Sam: monitoring note: enabling cpu-fallback increased tail latency for some long generations but avoided 500s. rolling rollback is possible if infra confirms driver fix.

Jordan: while infra looks, recommend we disable large-batch allocations and lower max context tokens for models on prod-gen-1 to reduce pressure when nodes come back. Patch ready: ```configs: { "max_batch_size": 8, "max_tokens": 1024 }```

Alex: agreed. applying conservative limits cluster-wide for affected pool.

Maya: node reboots scheduled by infra for gpu-node-09 and gpu-node-11. ETA 12m. will re-evaluate after driver update/reboot.

pagerduty: PDR-4027 acknowledged by Alex. Escalation level 1 -> on-call infra lead if nodes don't recover in 20m.

Sam: I'm handing off active mitigation to Jordan (next on-call window) in 30m. leaving notes: drained 09/11, scaled cpu-fallback to 10, routing patched for tenant-b, customer comms sent, infra ticket TKT-8743 created, saved logs to /artifacts/PDR-4027/ .

Jordan: taking over. I'll keep watch on driver/error rates and coordinate with infra. If nodes come back healthy, we'll gradually shift traffic back and undo rate limits.

Alex: quick checklist for handoff: - confirm infra driver update diff applied - ensure node kernel/drivers match our known-good image - verify KV cache warming on fallback pool - update status page when moving to partial recovery

Lee: noted. I'll update the status page once we observe steady <1% 5xx rate for 10m.

Maya: infra reports that NVIDIA driver 525.101.05 applied to nodes, reboot successful on gpu-node-11, gpu-node-09 still rebooting. monitoring shows no Xid-79 after reboot for 6m on 11.

Jordan: starting gradual re-intake: uncordon gpu-node-11, will let model-worker pods land with conservative limits.```kubectl uncordon gpu-node-11```

Maya: post-uncordon note: some containers showed transient cuda init errors but recovered. watch logs for repeated Xid entries.

Alex: if we don't see new Xid 79 or cuda alloc failures in next 15m, we can de-escalate PD and start moving non-critical traffic back.

pagerduty: PDR-4027 escalation held. Next escalation if incident remains active after 20m.

Jordan: marking this thread for follow-up postmortem. I'm collecting timestamps and metrics for incident timeline. assigned to Jordan for next 48h action item.

Sam: handing off fully. thanks team. :thumbsup:

Lee: updating stakeholders and marking support tickets as in-progress.

incident-bot: Incident PDR-4027 status: mitigated->partial (driver patched on 11, draining 09 in progress, traffic on fallback).

Alex: closing handoff. will reopen if we see recurrent driver resets.
